block.comment: Purpose: Stream a timed three-voice score from POLY.TXT. No whole melody buffer is needed. Hardware: use Connections to check pin ownership for your selected board. Open the comment bubbles on the main steps for explanations.
Declare one passive buzzer and its output pin. Use its name in later blocks. The AVR engine generates sound with Timer2 and supports up to three independent voices.
Declare one passive buzzer and its output pin. Use its name in later blocks. The AVR engine generates sound with Timer2 and supports up to three independent voices.
Declare one passive buzzer and its output pin. Use its name in later blocks. The AVR engine generates sound with Timer2 and supports up to three independent voices.
Map file voices 1, 2 and 3 to lead, bass and beat. Copy the supplied POLY.TXT onto the SD root. Same-time events overlap. The file header chooses absolute or delta milliseconds.
Runs once after power-on or reset. Initialise the program here; repeating measurements and animation belong in loop.
Keep servicing the file on every loop pass, without delays. At most 32 characters are read per call. Only one upcoming event is buffered; Timer2 drives all three buzzer outputs independently.
Repeats until power is removed. Each block runs in order, then execution returns to the top. Keep this loop responsive when servicing motors, music or serial input.
